classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that conjugate surds simplify in their sum and product, then use those two quantities in the standard quadratic construction formula.

content.prompt: Suppose the roots of a quadratic equation are $\sqrt3+\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt3-\sqrt2$. What is a faster method of forming the quadratic equation with these roots instead of expanding $(x-\sqrt3-\sqrt2)(x-\sqrt3+\sqrt2)$?

answer.short: Find the sum and product of the roots: $2\sqrt3$ and $1$. Then use $x^2-(\text{sum of roots})x+\text{product of roots}=0$, giving $x^2-2\sqrt3x+1=0$.
answer.worked:
Find the sum and product instead of expanding the factors involving $x$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta&=(\sqrt3+\sqrt2)+(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)\\\alpha+\beta&=2\sqrt3\\\alpha\beta&=(\sqrt3+\sqrt2)(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)\\\alpha\beta&=3-2=1.\end{align*}$$
The monic equation is $x^2-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha\beta=0$, so
$$x^2-2\sqrt3x+1=0.$$
